title: M4RM Gray-code table build (ILP + SIMD)
description:
Optimize the M4RM Gray-code table-build inner loop. Profiling shows it as a measurable fraction of M4RM total time, and its long dependent XOR chain leaves ILP cycles unused.

## Background

`crates/gf2-core/src/alg/m4rm.rs::build_gray_table` builds a $2^k$-row table by XORing successive rows in Gray-code order. The current implementation has a single accumulator threaded through every iteration, so the dependent XOR chain serializes the work and breaks the CPU's ability to issue multiple ops per cycle.

The fix walks PPC steps:

- V2 ILP: replace the single accumulator with 8 independent table accumulators so the dependent XOR chain breaks; each accumulator maintains its own Gray-code subsequence.
- V3 SIMD: batch the 8 accumulators across YMM lanes; reuse `LogicalFns::xor_fn` where possible.
- V6 prefetch: prefetch the next column block's rows while building the current Gray-table.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] M4RM end-to-end correctness unchanged (existing `m4rm.rs` tests pass).
- [hard] Sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact shows 8 independent accumulators after V2 and `vpxor` mnemonics after V3.
- [hard] No regression in M4RM total time on any size class measured by `m4rm_profile`.
- [hard] `perf stat -r 10` capture before/after recorded.
- [aspirational] $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean on the table-build sub-bench.

## Notes

Bench: `m4rm_profile` (existing, pinned by I1). Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
